seeds.text: Classify Orchestrator/runtime/UI actions by both confirmation level (none | light | strong | hard_gate) and reversibility (immediate_undo | compensating_action_only | non_reversible), replacing ad hoc per-surface confirmation behavior.

Adopt working interpretations: none = safe navigation/focus and low-risk presentation without user-data or live-runtime mutation; light = moderate-impact actions with plausible mis-clicks; strong = discard local state, remove artifacts/worktrees, revoke accepted state, or materially change live execution; hard_gate = canonical approval/blocked/HITL flows that generic UI cannot bypass.

Map action families: none — open/focus/navigate/deep-link, evidence/history/ledger/source control, tab-local filter/sort/search; light — minor acknowledge/dismiss, switch focused run, open resolution thread; strong — pause/cancel run, retry from safe point, prune worktree/clean workspace, prune evidence, revoke promotion, merge/split concerns; hard_gate — HITL approve/reject, graph patch application affecting canonical graph generation, remote-side-effect actions under explicit non-bypassable policy.

Use a shared governance/runtime record envelope: record_id, record_kind, project_id, optional run_id, scope refs (seam_id, package_id, node_id, attempt_id, promotion_id, concern_id, lane_id, worktree_id), status, created_at_utc, created_by_kind, created_by_ref, optional superseded_by_record_id, plus source_refs[], artifact_refs[], evidence_refs[], summary, optional detail_ref.

hard_gate confirmations must surface runtime-defined allowed actions, why the gate exists, exact consequence of each allowed action, and no hidden alternative path; strong confirmations must include reversibility class and whether local work/artifacts/history remain.
Do not label actions as Undo when the system only supports compensating paths; prefer labels such as Reopen, Restore, Retry from Safe Point, Create New Lane, Re-request Promotion, Reapply.
Delete Run in History remains questionable until delete semantics, authorization, and reversibility are defined relative to lineage and ledger records.

Confirmation behavior is implemented in many isolated places without a shared action policy across runtime, Orchestrator, Source Control, cleanup, and governance; documentation mixes revert, rollback, restore, and undo without a global distinction.
Destructive worktree and cleanup actions should preserve historical lineage in ledger/export metadata even when the live worktree or backing object is removed, so retired objects remain auditable.
Cross-check action/confirmation work against Plans/storage-plan.md, Orchestrator_Page.md, Contracts_V0.md, FinalGUISpec.md, Run_Graph_View.md for evidence vs artifact vs record distinctions.

Review record direction: review_id, review kind (package | seam | verifier), target scope refs, reviewer identity, criteria/profile, findings summary, finding/concern refs, verdict, linked artifacts/evidence, timestamps; findings may nominate concerns but the review record stays distinct from concern records.

Corroboration: split corroboration_request/packet (claim, scope, trigger, evidence set, quorum model, actors) from corroboration_result (participant outputs, quorum, accepted/advisory outcome, downstream concern/promotion/patch implications).

Graph patch: graph_patch_request (patch point, issue/concern refs, structural change summary, affected generation, requester) vs graph_patch_result (old/new generation, invalidated/surviving path refs, downstream implications).

Promotion record: promotion class (lane_to_package, package_to_seam, seam_completion), source/target scope, eligibility at decision time, blocking/concern refs, review/corroboration refs, decision outcome, revocation/reopen lineage.

Recovery record: recovery kind (safe-point restore, restart reconciliation, blocked prerequisite resolution, lane/worktree restore), scope refs, trigger, preconditions, result, attempt/run linkage, affected concern refs.

State transition report: from/to state, target object, actor/source, rationale, prerequisite evidence/review/corroboration refs, resulting downstream obligations — shared exact record to avoid bespoke decision-summary fields per family.
Record = canonical structured ledger/export/search object; artifact = file/blob/renderable output linked from the record (e.g., review markdown summary is artifact; review record is ledger object).
Export contracts should use the record envelope as manifest backbone; artifact files attach by reference rather than replacing record structure.

Many exact record families are assumed in product docs but not shaped consistently; artifacts are documented more concretely than governing record objects, leaving search, deep links, and ledger exact-record views awkward.
Export seam: storage-plan.md, FinalGUISpec.md, Orchestrator_Page.md, usage-feature.md, Widget_System.md.

Distinguish export modes: record export (exact structured objects, canonical ids, references, metadata), bundle export (manifest + records + attached artifacts/blobs/files), and view export (filtered table/list/chart convenience representation).
Orchestrator export manifest (part 1): export_id, export_kind, project_id, optional run_id and focused_run_id, generated_at_utc — every non-trivial Orchestrator export should include a manifest.

Expected export families: Evidence, Artifact, Ledger, Run, and single exact-record export; Ledger record-shaped first with CSV/JSON as projections; Run export bundles run metadata, exact records, linked artifacts/evidence, and historical/superseded flags.

Orchestrator export language still does not pin canonical manifest, record- vs view-shaped payloads, packaging of artifacts/records/refs, or explicit behavior for historical/superseded/removed backing objects.

Orchestrator export manifest (part 2): source_surface, filter_summary, record_counts, artifact_counts, included_record_ids[], included_artifact_ids[], status_notes, schema_version — so bundles stay inspectable and auditable.

Exact-record surfaces must export canonical records, not UI-transformed rows: Ledger export preserves canonical ids and structured fields; JSON/JSONL stays close to canonical record shape; CSV is a convenience projection only.
Exports must preserve historical truth when live backing objects are gone (e.g., removed worktree or retired graph path) — absence of live files must not corrupt exported record bundles.
view export (filtered ledger CSV, concern table CSV, chart export) must be explicitly labeled non-canonical convenience; not treated as archival format.

Exporting an artifact alone must retain enough metadata to identify originating record, run, and object; evidence export should include evidence records, linked artifact refs, summaries, and concern/review/corroboration linkage when present.
Orchestrator-specific export contracts remain underspecified on canonical manifest, record- vs view-shape packaging, and behavior for superseded/removed backing objects beyond general principles.
Config bundle export/import is explicit while Orchestrator usage/evidence export language is too UI-view-centric; no obvious shared Orchestrator export-manifest contract.

Settings/runtime presentation must keep three axes distinct: source axis (inherit/override / where value came from), request axis (what the run asked for), execution/result axis (honored/skipped/clamped effective outcome).
Canonical display groups: Inherited from, Overridden by, Requested, Effective, Reason, Support — with examples tying config source, requested model, effective model, and per-control support states.

Surface routing: Settings — source-axis heavy (what will be requested from here); Orchestrator/graph/run detail — request and execution-axis heavy (what was asked vs what happened); Progress — compact requested/effective; History/Ledger — audit trail of requested/effective + reason + source snapshot refs; Authentication/Usage — effective account/auth emphasis with policy disclosure.
Historical run views must show frozen requested/effective state from that run; current settings/inheritance elsewhere must not overwrite historical audit rows.
UI must show the winning configuration source for Persona, provider/model/variant/effort, auth mode, account policy, and worker policy — users should not reconstruct precedence from documentation.
Settings override seam: Multi-Account.md, Models_System.md, Prompt_Pipeline.md, Personas.md, FinalGUISpec.md, Orchestrator_Page.md, storage-plan.md.

Requested/effective is well defined in runtime docs, but inherited/override presentation is not unified across settings surfaces; users will confuse current settings winner, requested run state, and effective runtime result without a shared grammar.
Manual override lifecycle is explicit for Persona, but similar presentation rules are less explicit for provider/model/account/worker-policy overrides.
Preserve the global requested-Persona precedence chain while requiring each surface auto resolver to emit a deterministic ranked candidate set plus structured explanation metadata.

Orchestrator auto-resolver inputs should include actor type (package/seam overseer, node worker, verifier, corroborator, recovery, graph patch planner), work/operation type (implementation, review, integration, corroboration, recovery, planning/patching), scope level (seam/package/node/attempt), and project hints (languages, frameworks, domain traits, GUI/backend/infra emphasis).

Inside the auto resolver, prioritize: hard requirements from plan/tier/surface contract, then actor-type bias, operation-type bias, scope bias, language/framework/domain hints, project defaults, then final fallback; actor and operation type should dominate stack hints so reviewers are not silently remapped to coding personas.

Bias Orchestrator defaults by role: package overseer toward package-local delivery/readiness; seam overseer toward cross-package integration truth; node worker toward implementation matched to stack; verifier/reviewer and corroborator toward distinct review/challenge personas; recovery toward troubleshooting; graph patch planner toward planning/architecture — exact persona ids may evolve but mapping policy should be explicit.

Retain Prompt Pipeline clarification rule: if two same-tier candidates remain and the system cannot choose deterministically, ask for clarification rather than speculating — rare in Orchestrator but still needed for ambiguous manual natural-language requests.

When preferred Persona is unavailable after capability/provider/model filtering, fall through deterministically; record requested Persona, effective Persona, selection reason, and skipped Persona controls; only hard requirements warrant stronger blocking.
Orchestrator auto-resolver remains qualitative: docs list project/language/domain/framework/tier/operation inputs but do not fully prioritize them relative to actor/work-type biases.
Without a sharper actor-type mapping, auto Persona risks feeling arbitrary in the rewrite model where overseer roles dominate; global precedence chain is clear but Orchestrator specifics are not.

Scoped overrides for task/run/subagent must prevent package defaults leaking across unrelated runs and subagent overrides becoming package defaults; historical runs retain frozen effective Persona independent of later config changes.
Persona resolution seam: Personas.md, Prompt_Pipeline.md, interview-subagent-integration.md, Models_System.md, orchestrator-subagent-integration.md, FinalGUISpec.md.
